utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar would you -- there is French translation on channel 4. That has been changed by now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No problem. Thank you. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Liborius, I would like to remind you, as I did during the past days, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court wanted to deal with the housekeeping matter that we ended with yesterday or should I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Court still has not given up hope that we might finish because we will continue Friday afternoon and we will stop at 6.00, and we'll see how far we come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been advised by the staff of the witness assistance section that I should leave at 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your plane, as far as I understand, leaves at 8.30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 8.00 I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received other information. We'll check that. But if it would be 8.00, that would be three hours and even perhaps three and a half hours. We will check that and we'll take care that you'll not miss your plane. At least we'll do everything in order to avoid that, whether you need to leave at 5.00 or 6.00 for those purposes -- Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One housekeeping matter that have is we played a video of Kricke at the end of the session yesterday. I'm advised that there was some change because the number that I called up was still a tentative P number. We have done a clip, we've cut it to the clip that we actually showed in court and have a -- uploaded it and have a D number for it and I would propose that we give -- we, the Defence, tender that clip into evidence and it is 1D50-0377.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the clip that ends where we see the Kricke --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The sign, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D750.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Waespi. D750 is admitted into evidence. We later will deal with the outstanding list of exhibits, Prosecution Exhibits. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to start where we left off yesterday. And as you will recall, I had asked you questions about how -- when you were doing these patrols you were able to determine what was a Croat village -- Croat majority village versus a Serb majority village and whether damage had occurred before or after the 4th of August, 1995. And in the transcript at page 8432 to 8433, you indicated that the way you would be able to tell was from previous information before Operation Storm, from the Regional Centre Knin with its ECMM teams had throughout the war covered the whole area. And then on page 8434 you said: "Usually we would relate to the information that was gathered by the teams prior to Operation Storm; secondly, we would relate to the government of Croatia's statistics for each municipality. The big blue book on municipality structures." So are those the two principle means by which you were able to tell the difference between a Serb majority village and a Croat majority village when doing these patrols?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you a few examples of -- of this off my head how we would work. I'm sure that in the preparations of our patrols, if there were other relevant information available, we would take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if could I have P811 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, this is the daily report of the 22nd of August, 1995, and you and Mr. Hendriks are the authors of it. Now, the villages down below as well as on the next page are the results of the patrol you and Mr. Hendriks did on that day, and I'm going to ask you now to look at the list and -- and tell me if I'm interpreting the list correctly. For example, if you look six villages in, it says Polaca. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. It says totally damaged by 1991 war, DPs returning. Am I right to assume that what that means is that this is a village that had been damaged prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You obviously were, as you were doing these patrols, noting which villages were damaged but -- you believed had been destroyed or damaged prior to Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question says, as we were doing the patrols noting which villages we believe, I mean, we believe -- what we did was to have a reference later, while we were doing our patrols -- we noted down what we saw, interviewed people, if we could, and then we would see the information that was available to us. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me follow up --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question seems to suggest that we were doing the match, so to speak, while we were on patrol. Am I right to assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That wasn't what I intended. Let me follow up on what you just said while giving the court reporter a --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please put your question again so I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We need to pause, just to remind you again, between my questions and your answers so that the court reporter and the interpreters have a fair chance. Let me put it a different way. When you gathered this information during the day and then by the time you prepared the daily report of your activities, you tried to assess which villages were damaged prior to Operation Storm and include that in your daily report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of our abilities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So we see that one entry for Polace which indicates that the damage in that village had occurred prior to Operation Storm. The rest of the entries, then, I interpret that you believed the damage occurred during or after Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our impression at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if I could have D743 on the screen, please. And if we could go to what is marked on the bottom as 1D50-0245, please. That's not the right page, so ... there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Liborius, I don't know if you can see the screen there, but that is the notebook and the notes you took on the 22nd of August. Feel free to refer to the hard copy that you have in front of you, the original. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just read us the first few lines of what you've written down there.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Task, W part of AOR, out 0820, up Zadar, kilometre 5335, in 1500, 900; Whiskey Juliette 3883; Biljane TD, utilities electricity at work, electrical wiring. 9.30, S for Benkovac. [Foreign language spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you translate that for us?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Life normal, people, house okay. Arrow, DP return. Whiskey Juliette 4774, Mikulici Sopot 0939. Zapuzane, Whiskey, Juliette 4473.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We can stop right there. First can you tell me, for example, when you say 0900, 0930, 0939, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would usually be time-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you can go through the notes, Mr. Liborius, and flip through the pages. I assume that all those time entries reflect the time that were in the villages that are then reflected in the daily report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if I could have 1D50-0367.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, what we've done is we have created charts to show, based on your notebook and based on your daily report, the path that you would have travelled on the 22nd, given the time-frames and the villages that you were in, and if you -- I don't know if can you do it 13 years later, but does that indicate to you - and we can turn the page to the next page. Now, what we've done there is classify according to the classifications that are in your daily report and in your notebook, we've colour-coded the villages and put in where you entered a time we put all those times in. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And for example the green colour coding is Polace which is in the middle part of your screen all the way to the far left. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So that would be a village that you were in that was destroyed before Operation Storm according to your daily report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could flip to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What we tried to reconstruct based on the times that you were in these villages is the distance between the villages and the travel speed that you would had to be going at various speeds and how much territory you could cover. And if you look through this and compare it with your notes, is it fair to say you, for the most part when you visiting these villages, you were sticking to the main road and not actually going into the villages. You were just driving through the main road and what you could see to the left or to the right of the road is what you would record in the patrol notebook?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would depend on the information we had about the area, how we would tailor the individual patrol. And if you suggest, if I get your question right, that we would travel by the main roads between the points, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, what I understood from your notes, and you correct me if I'm wrong, for example, Guglete is the last entry there. On the chart on your screen, as well as in your notebook, it is roughly 12.15. What I understood from your notes, sir, is generally speaking you would be in a moving vehicle making observations and if something caught your attention, as, for example, in Guglete you would then stop the car and check for something specific. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Guglete. Where are we ... I can't find Guglete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Guglete is the third page of your 22 August entry at the top.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Sorry repeat, Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You tell me if I explained this correctly. Your general practice was to drive on a main road and record what you see on the left and the right, and that if something of particular interest caught your attention, you may stop in a particular village, as you did there Guglete, for example, where it appeared that you had an extended stay?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So for many of these villages this is what you observed on the main roads going left and right without actually going into the villages, while Guglete may be an example where you actually stopped in the village and made observations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the patrol patterns, there was a difference, as I said again, depending on the situation, some places we would have information from other agencies. At the 22nd of August we had already been on the road for some time. Colleagues had also been. Sometimes we would stay; sometimes we would drive relatively faster having observed what was previously informed to us. Some places we would stop. So I cannot really say that there was only one particular way of doing the monitoring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But certainly for some of the villages entered, this is an observation based on being in a moving vehicle passing through on a main road. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the observations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could go back to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I can't tell you at this point in time precisely when did we stop, how long the stop was. The purpose of this book was not to say where are we at a particular time. The purpose of it was to note down information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, can we go to the second page of this exhibit, please. If you look at the time sequencing, for example Donje Biljana, 9.00 a.m. 9.30 you're in Mikulici. 9.39 you're in Polace or Zapuzane. 9.58 you've come back and now you're in Podlug. 10.20 you're in Gornje Ceranje. 10.30 you're in Budak. You can reconstruct, sir, can't you from where you were at various points in the day how much time could have possibly been spent in these particular villages?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a plus or minus, I'm not sure whether the exact route, if you look to the east of Budak would that be. I can't tell you today. Sometimes we would take the fastest road returning back, and I cannot today say that it was the exact route, for example, east of Budak, 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, otherwise, it seems to make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, what we've done, Mr. Liborius, is we took that Croatian census of the ethnic break down of the villages that you visited, and then compared and colour-coded them with what you found on your patrol on the 22nd of August. And you'll note again you did make the notation in Polace where you thought that the damage was prior to Operation Storm in green, on this chart; and according to the census Polace was a Croat majority village, as can you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now from what I gather, for example, if we look at the middle portion of the screen off to the right you'll see Medvidja. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is it coloured pink, because in your notebook it is entered -- and in your daily report it is entered as totally destroyed. Which is, according to the census a majority Croat village. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Lisicic is below Medvidja and in the left. It is also categorised by you in your daily report as totally destroyed. Lisicic had 479 Croats and two Serbs, according to the census. There is another village, Pridraga which is up to the left in blue, in the upper part of this page, which you also --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- identified as totally destroy, a village with 1770 Croats and two Serbs. Now, my first question to you, sir, is based on what you've just answered, that to the best of your ability you did try to identify villages that had been destroyed prior to Operation Storm, as indicated by the green colour coating of coding of Polace, what we should conclude from your daily report is that these Croat villages were burned down after Operation Storm, or during Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we observed was recent burning. We did not include in the daily report, if could you please produce that again, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That would be P811.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I'll just help you out here. I have given you three villages.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if you can look at them - if we can scroll down a little bit more, Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you see there is that we do not include whether it was a Serb or Croat village. Your question, and that's the reason why I ask you, I'm not sure I fully understand it, that you say it's a Croat village, yes, it was, according to the census in 1991, if you have so checked. And of course it was very unfortunate that from Croat majority villages that they were expelled during RSK times. But we did not include, as you see in the report there, the notion whether it was Croat villages or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question, sir, was there are three villages that I have given to you, and if you look on your screen it is D, Viduka, which I have identified for you as Croat majority. If you look farther down, Medvidja --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And -- what was the other one - Lisicic, which is on the next page?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's on the next page, last entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please. Up top. Lisicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For example totally burned, deserted?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question to you is: The first thing that Trial Chamber should include is that your assessment was that that village was burned recently, meaning after the 4th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. The second step is that given the population census of 1991, the Trial Chamber, according to you, should find that this village, which was -- let me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes I believe the witness said that the -- he didn't know at that time. He made his factual observation as to damage or not whether the village predominantly Croatian or Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I asked him if in preparing the daily reports then they would try to do that, and he said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Misetic you suggest to the witness things that we should believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll change it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's, of course, not what the witness is supposed to do and that's not what we the Chamber expects a witness to day. The reason is for the Chamber the factual observations for the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have now established that Lisicic was burned -- or should say totally burned and deserted after the 4th of August. My question to you, sir, is: It was your understanding that a Croat majority village from 1991 was burned down after Operation Storm. You knew that when you put the report together on the 22nd of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this report was -- sorry. That report was a factual listing of the observations we made during that patrol. Now, of course, where we had a chance - sometimes we did, sometime there were nobody, sometimes time was -- was scarce - we tried to speak with -- with people. Of course, in some of the villages a significant change of population took place during the Krajina years. That was the reason why, in the daily reports, we would remain factual. If it had been -- the houses had been intact before Operation Storm, to the best of our knowledge, and that we, on the 22nd of August, found it totally burnt, recently burnt, deserted, we would note so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to see whether we can get some clarity in here. What Mr. Misetic actually is asking you is the following. Where you noted, only for one village that it was totally destroyed in 1991, and you did not note that, in relation to other villages, that Mr. Misetic is surprised that villages of a Croat majority are not noted as being destroyed at an earlier stage and one of the implicit assumptions is that Mr. Misetic would not expect the Croats to fully destroy their own villages in 1995. That's the implicit suggestion. Further, Mr. Misetic is using the word "majority" sometimes pointing at a close to 100 per cent majority, sometimes to a 60 per cent/40 per cent majority, he puts that all together. Now, do you have an answer to what apparently is on Mr. Misetic's mind that you did not note the destruction of majority or almost 100 percent Croatian villages as done in earlier stages, and Mr. Misetic, for that reason wonders whether your observations were accurate. Could you please respond to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As it is a question that I see contains some different elements, I will try to cover them all. And I think, actually, that I have a recollection of that particular village that Mr. Misetic is referring to. The old destruction done prior to Operation Storm, 1991, would have another appearance as to recent destruction done very recently. I gather that is one of the elements in the answer. Second element, the -- as was mentioned, the implicit suggestions why we do not note down, that it is to say, a 1991 Croatian majority village, that was not really the purpose of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, that was not my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was why you did not note down for majority Croatian villages that they were destroyed in -- well, prior before Operation Storm, and therefore is the implicit assumption, that the Croats would not destroy totally their own villages. So Mr. Misetic cannot understand that this damage total destruction of villages would take place in 1995. He has difficulties to understand and believe that. Nevertheless, he does not find in your report that the damage to these villages was done far before Operation Storm, that's what is bothering Mr. Misetic. And therefore majority Croat village is not -- he is focussing on villages which on the basis of the census appear to be in 1991 majority Croatian villages; and, nevertheless, there is no clue to early destruction and there is a suggestion of recent destruction. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me then help. What we came across was that the burning did take place, and I think that the -- if you wish, the missing link is the population change. I perfectly see that there is no reason why you should burn what previously had Croatian majority population. Nevertheless, what we saw was that a significant population change had taken place during the war. And, for one reason or another, those houses, in many instances there would be living Serbs in them, were then burned. What we observed was that they were burnt totally or partly, deserted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to see whether I understand you, because it is important that you understand the questions and the answers as well. What you're actually saying is that what was a majority Croatian village in 1991 might not have been a majority Croatian village anymore in 1995, due to the fact that a Serb population may have gone into that village. That's what you're telling me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In many instances, that was the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic, I'm trying to understand everything, and to understand the answers and verify whether I understood them well because that seems to be a problem now and then. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one question. One of the matters you have not answered is whether the notation of destruction far before Operation Storm, if that is not there, do you think your observations were and the notations were always accurate, or do you guarantee for the accuracy of the -- not noting that it was the early destruction? Do you think that not noting that it was early destruction gives us reliable information as to the time of the destruction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In most instances, yes. My observations were made to the very best of our abilities at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic, there's another matter. I don't know whether you're going to pursue this on the basis of one report only or on the basis of all of the reports because for the reliability of the information of course an overall view would assist the Chamber best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I had given the time. I chose two and I believe he did -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. You did choose them at random?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Well, I mean as I look through his notebook he went on the 18th, 22nd, 23rd, and 24th, and I believe the 25th. I took two of them because they were -- I didn't want to go through every day, but at some point it is my position that it's the job of the Prosecution to come back then with these statistics and figure out and make some sense of all of this, but I will continue to pursue this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I want to be clear on this, based on your answers that you have now given to the Presiding Judge, Mr. Liborius. First of all, if it is not noted that the village was destroyed in 1991, that means that your observation was that the village was destroyed after Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking for the -- interjection in the Judge's ... Could we scroll a bit up -- no, sorry. We just a few lines up, please, so I can see the Judge's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is now Mr. Misetic, his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "So the absence of information, whether it was destroyed" -- sorry, "the absence of 1991 or prior to Operation Storm should in general be seen as indication that it was done after Operation Storm." Do I read you right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in most case, yes. In most cases. I will not exclude that there will be some instances where it was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you think of a single time that you thought the damage had occurred prior to Operation Storm but decided not to note that in a daily report?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would in general try to get as much information in, of course, within reasonable time resources and so on, and you should take into consideration the amount of destruction, and it was going on as we were there, it compelled us to make the best judgements we could at that time. If there would be a couple of houses, if there would be some quarters of a -- as you indicate in your map, a town where there were both Serbs and Croats, some destruction had taken place before, some had been rebuilt, some then were burned again because sometimes it was also the revenge, that a previously Croat owned house would be rebuilt by the Serbs during the Krajina years and then destroyed. That can blur the picture. And I'm not going to say that everything single house in every single village that we can trace that either before or after. This is a condensed impression of a very large area, being destroyed as we were witnessing it and as we were noting in our reports to the best of our abilities. I excuse the long answer, but that is a reflection, I believe, of the whole truth of the reflection that we are having in our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I let you get the long response, now I'm going to go back to the question I posed. Can you think of a single time that you thought the damage you saw had occurred prior to Operation Storm but you decided not to note that fact in a daily report. It's a yes or no answer, Mr. Liborius?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I have great problems with this question. The witness - and I do understand that you are focusing to take him back to the question - was that sometimes in villages there was damage which was -- may have inflicted earlier, then rebuilding then -- so, therefore, the damage you saw, we should make that clear, did it ever happen or do you have any recollection that you may have seen villages in which you saw early destruction of an early date well before Operation Storm, where you have not noted that down? For example, in circumstances as you described which is that you saw some old damage, some new damage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did have some of the reports dealing with the question of the possibilities of return, and in order to assess that possibility in the area, we could have to observe whether they were inhabitable houses, how large a percentage or so, so, yes there could be instances. In our longer reports, some of which I believe have been tendered into evidence here, we developed that discussion, how are the possibilities for return. In doing that we did not have to relate to whether it was a majority Croat; so, yes, there would be instances where there would be destruction prior to Operation Storm, but in these daily -- in this patrol -- we have patrol report we have here, the -- the pre-1991 mention is, at that time, to the best of our abilities, the only one done before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you may have understood that the damage you observed when we're talking about one village in view of the previous answer of the witness was not a basis on which, in my view, you could put that question. We have -- the witness has answered whether he has answered the question, I leave it up to you to see whether you are satisfied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the interests of time, Your Honour, I would like to go back to 1D50-0367, please. And we can go to the third page again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, for example, if we look at yellow, undamaged villages, we have in the upper right-hand corner yellow blocks, Komazeci, with the hamlets with V. Varos Komazeci valley. And they are undamaged villages which were 100 percent Serb. Zapuzane, which is in the middle of the page all the way to the left. If you follow it there's a yellow block there. In 1991 there were nine Croats and 532 Serbs, and the village when you saw it on the 22nd of August, was undamaged. My question now is: You were doing this to make an assessment of the situation. Did you ever think to include in your assessments where you actually noted in the daily reports that you found undamaged villages, to note that this was a -- an exclusively Serb village, or almost exclusively Serb village, with respect to these two villages?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, the assessment at a larger scale would be done at the RC level. Sometimes we would include it; sometimes not. What we did see sometimes was that the partly destroyed villages were then later destroyed. And that -- that compilation of information was also done at a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm focussed right now on the 22nd of August and your preparation of the daily report. So I have showed you two exclusively Serb villages, or almost exclusively Serb villages. If we go to other undamaged villages, Sopot, which is Mikulici which is in that general area, which is Sopot - sorry - upper left-hand, far left, Mikulici, Podlug, and Perusic. Perusic is on the bottom of the screen on the right-hand side. These are undamaged villages with sizeable Serbian minorities in them. My question to you, sir, specifically for the 22nd of August, you are in a fact-finding role on that day. You're preparing a daily report. Did you think it was important to note where you found Serbian villages or villages with sizeable Serbian minorities that were undamaged, to make that note as well in the daily report?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is not in the daily report, in that particular daily report, it was not apparently felt that it should be included. That is not to suggest that that information, if that is in your question, would not be conveyed on. There would be other reports for that purpose. This -- and I'm afraid I have to say it again. The purpose of the report was to establish what we had seen on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not to discuss whether it was a Serb majority or it was a Croat or what has happened during the population movement during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, I'm going to get --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, no, it is not in the report. Therefore, it was apparently not considered important enough for that particular daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We're going to get to this issue in a moment and I'm going to tell you why we're going through this exercise, so you can prepare to give me an answer when we get to that point. These daily reports were used to compile your 26 August report, in which you, if I may use the word, give an almost apocalyptic assessment of what is happening in Sector South. You specifically note that 60 to 80 per cent of the housing in Sector South had been burned down using this information. Now, we're going through this exercise to see the methodology you used in gathering the information. Given that you are the author of the 22nd August daily report along with Mr. Hendriks, my question to you is: At any time between 22nd of August and the submission of the 26 August report, did you write down and note Serbian villages or villages with sizeable Serbian minorities that were undamaged?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would refer you to the daily reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a question here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... yes. I think, as a matter of fact that if have you any questions at the end of your testimony, of course you can put them. This is not debate or a discussion. This is an examination. So, therefore, you have paper, and so if there's any question that remains, please write it down and at the end you will have an opportunity to raise any issue you consider not to be covered sufficiently. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One question, and again it relates to the fact that we heard a lot of your conclusions on direct examination, your 26 August report is submitted, you gave an assessment, I believe, that what happened in August was much more professionally done in light of the speed than what the reports did in four years. So I'd like to ask you, sir, given the fact that you've made some assessments, let's look at this picture, let's take the picture on 22nd of August as you saw it then. And tell me what you conclude, when you find, according to your own testimony, three majority Croat or exclusively Croat villages destroyed after Operation Storm, according to you, two exclusively Serbian villages undamaged, three villages with sizeable Serbian minorities undamaged, and I can also point out to you that there are also villages here with sizeable -- with Croat majorities which you've identified as partly damaged. Given this picture, tell us what you concluded? What's happening on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought I was here to give evidence of what I saw. If I'm now asked to make a conclusion, based on your information here, that is not what I did in the daily report. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw was that a lot of burning took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the conclusion you're trying to talk me into to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Liborius, "the conclusion you're trying to talk me into" is not something for you to comment. If the Chamber feels that you're unfairly dealt with by Mr. Misetic, first of all, Mr. Waespi will object against the question; second, the Chamber exercises control, as you may have noticed meanwhile, over the examination of witnesses. Mr. Misetic, at the same time, asking for conclusions if there are any conclusions drawn by the witness at the time which you would like to challenge, no problem. To invite the witness to draw conclusions where he is supposed primarily to testify on facts might not greatly assist the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm only doing it because there was no problem with drawing conclusions on direct examination, and specifically he has tendered a report from the 26th of August --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may take him to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the report of the 26th, no problem with that. At the same time, to some extent the Chamber leaves the examination of witnesses to the parties. Not in every respect. And I take it that you have observed how the Chamber has intervened during this testimony of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I tender this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, of course we have to accept for the time being that these population figures are accurate for the time relevant. That's 1995 and I have no information that this is correct. So given that reservation, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is -- we disclosed precisely for this reason when we released our documents to the Prosecution. They have the 1991 census figures upon which this exhibit is based. I don't intend to tender the exhibit, but I did want to give it to the Prosecution so they can review it and check.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. And of course there is a difference between the state of population in 1991 and 1995 as you also heard from the witness. But I do have no objections to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe I was clear, Your Honour, that I'm referring -- these are 1991 statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear to me, certainly, of course. Some questions are still there, for example, just as Biljsana [phoen] is concerned, there apparently are four villages but where we have -- or at least hamlets, but we do not have the -- yes, since there are only four Croats, there could not be more than four in one hamlet. That's for clear which doesn't make a majority anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me just state for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber -- one of the things that comes into my mind whether a complete analysis of all the data would not be something that would assist the Chamber. For this moment, there's no objection, Mr. Waespi, if have you got until Monday to make any further observations in relation to the data included here, and Madam Registrar meanwhile could you provide a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just to make a point. Of course we can readily ascertain, and I believe Mr. Misetic that these are 1991 data. What is impossible for me to do, even until Monday, is to check whether these are relate the data to -- of the same 1995, which I understand the Defence doesn't claim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It goes without saying that the source for the numbers here is the 1991 census. We have heard the testimony of the witness, we have -- we can think about all this, and we have to evaluate and interpret the whole of it. That goes without saying. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D751.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D751 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Waespi, if there are any objections I would like to hear that not later than by Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, two points to make here. Just for the future, the hamlets were not counted separately in the 1991 census figures. The villages were, just for future reference. Secondly, I think the Gotovina Defence will stipulate that on the eve of Operation Storm there were virtually no Croats in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Madam Registrar if we could have 1D50-0191 -- I'm sorry 1D50-0191, yes. Sorry. 1D50-0372. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, without taking you through your 18 August daily report, unless wish to see it, we've done the same thing for your patrol on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I wish to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: P809, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is your daily report for the 18th of August, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can scroll to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see the list of villages there, and it continues on to the next page. When you're ready, we can turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I note again the first entry on the second page, Jare, you make the identification of a village that you concluded was damaged prior to Operation Storm. Correct.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I note that there are no other similar qualifications for any of the other villages identified here. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And from your previous answers to my questions, we should conclude that your conclusion on -- at the end of the day on the 18th August was that all of these villages except for Jare were villages that had been -- and that are identified specifically as having been burned were burned after Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to peruse my notes before --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go to the previous page, please, of the daily report. Oh. Could we ... Yes, I see from my patrol notebook that during that day, we out and -- and talking with different people, some places we find no people. And in reference to Jare, as you ask about, I did note in my patrol notebook that it has been destroyed in 1991, 1992. We passed a check-point, and I cannot see from my notes whether we were talking with people to get this information, destroyed in 1991, 1992. The information in my patrol notebook indicates that there were different sources of information. Our own observation, talking with people. So I can only say that Jare -- it would indicate that we had been talk with people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. My question, again, sir, was that's what you entered for Jare. For the rest of the villages there is no qualification that they were burnt prior to Operation Storm, and, therefore, we should conclude that your finding on that day was that these were villages that were burnt after Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In many instances, yes, with the understanding, as I said before, that also here we are out to check whether it is feasible to return people and how the -- the corpus of houses, accommodation, what the status is. So, again, I won't repeat the discussion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, if a notation here -- let's just ask it this way: In this daily report, if it is not noted that a village was burnt prior to Operation Storm, should that be interpreted to mean that your finding was that it was burnt after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most instances, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which instances on this report should it not be interpreted that way?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer that question, I need to look at my notes. [Foreign language spoken] Could we go to the next page, please. Kosora. In Bicelic. Do we have Bicelic in -- no, sorry. Yes, in most instances, it would indicate that. I would, however, also say that when this was taking place in the front line area, previous front line area, as we know the pink zone south of the original UN-defined area, we were in areas where, again, the repopulation in the pink zones, the repopulation issue was in particular delicate. Therefore, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Listening to you, I assume that the answer to the question, Which instances on this report should it not be interpreted that way, that your answer would be, I can't identify any of the instances in this report where it should be understood in a different way. That, from many words, I understand is your answer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now if we could turn to 1D50-0372?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is -- the white lines are the patrol you took on that day. The brown line is the international border. So at some point you crossed over the international border and went into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We've done the same thing again based on the notebook entries that have you for that date, starting at 11.01, and there are two entries there because I believe in your notebook it's unclear whether you mean Djurici or Turici. So we put both in there. There are two places in that general area. One is called Turici, the other is called Djuric, we weren't able to decipher your notes. So we're giving you both on the screen there. And you can see the various ways at the various times it would appear from the timing you took that road, you went all the way down south, you turned around, you went back up. At 1408 you're in Vuci Polje, and continued on up, you went back to Kijevo, and in 1543, at the top middle of the page, you crossed over and you into Unista in Bosnia. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now again we've done the colour coding, deserted and burnt we've put in pink. Jare, which you identified as being destroyed before Operation Storm, is in green. The yellow marks the undamaged village that you found, and this is from both the sitrep and in your notes -- I'm sorry, in the sitrep undamaged. And in the grey we've put villages and hamlets not in the sitrep but that are referenced in your -- it says diary should say your notebook. Now, if we can turn the page, please. In addition to the green, Jare, which is part of -- which is a hamlet in the Vinalic [phoen] village, which was 100 per cent Croat in 1991 and which you did properly identify as being destroyed prior to Operation storm, you will note at the top middle of the page when you crossed over into Bosnia, there was a totally deserted and burnt majority Croat village, Kijevo, middle left hand above the box there with the classifications, Kijevo. Totally deserted and burnt, which was almost a 100 per cent Croatian village in 1991. Dabar, which is towards the -- as you travel south down the road. I don't know if you can see it, along that line towards the end of that trip down south there's a pink box. Dabar is also a majority Croat village that was deserted and burnt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I earlier commented on what is a majority. Of course 61 against 59 is still a majority, but you could also describe it as of mixed population. I see for Dabar, 64 against 55 which is not as cruel as 61 against 59, but to say "majority" is at least -- gives an impression which is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, for my purposes, Your Honour, the allegation is the village was completely burnt after Operation Storm, and if there were -- even if you call it a mixed population village, my inference that I'm going to ask you to draw is still the same. [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't understand, but from a factual point of view I think it is fair to say it is a mix the population with a Croat majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You have on that road down south in the middle, Koljane, which is the village but Dragovic is the hamlet which you identified in the sitrep undamaged which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to phrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Try to do your best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- majority Serb village that was undamaged on your route. And I have the same questions that I had with the other analysis of your patrol. Why didn't you note that the deserted and burnt villages that we see in pink there and that are either majority Croat or mixed population, why didn't you note that those were the classifications of the village?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You ask why we did not note that those were the classifications of the villages. We didn't really have that classification. It was a matter of observing whether it was partly destroyed, destroyed, or not destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to try to get to my next point in this topic area, so I'm going to tender this exhibit right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same reservation, I take it, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number D752.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D752. And you have the same time limit, Mr. Waespi, for making the further submissions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, may I have P810 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the list of villages that you prepared dated 22 August, 1995. Can you look -- let's say the first page and determine -- let's look at just the villages that are deserted and burnt or totally destroyed. Tell me which of these villages is majority Serb or majority Croat or mixed population?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: First a correction. I did not prepare that report. It is dated Zadar, the 22nd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would believe that the RC staff in Zadar prepared it. It would be then prepared from the input from the ECMM teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you, looking at this page, how would you go about determining now which of these villages are destroyed or totally burnt are majority Serbian villages?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You ask me how I would go about determining now which of these villages are destroyed as majority Serbian villages. Majority in 1991, I would refer -- I would look in the census, as I said, the reference book. I think in general it was not disputed. Whether it was changed, the population, during the war, we have been through that discussion. So if you ask me how I would go about determining, I think that satisfies the question or -- the purpose of the report there was to give an overview of the level of destruction. You indicated in one of your earlier questions that we had written that 60 to 80 per cent of the property in the -- in the -- that part of the Sector South had a been destroyed. That is a factual observation. It is a mathematical exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You agree with me then that there is no way for you to look at this page and determine which of the villages that have been described as burnt or totally destroyed are majority Serbian villages in the 1991 census, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I'll relate to the reference books I told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you asking the witness whether he could do it now or whether he could do it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both. Then let's try to make that clear. Could you at the time -- first of all, can you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not without the reference material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I had the reference material, I would through many hours of study be able to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, let's move to P815, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the summary, Mr. Liborius. This is your report. "In the period from the 7th to the 24th of August 1995, three ECMM teams observed a systematic destruction, mainly by burning, of property in the former RSK areas. A rough estimate is that between 60 to 80 per cent of the property in former UN Sector South have been fully or partly destroyed. The burnings were to a very large extent carried out by uniformed HV soldiers under command inside areas where access was strictly controlled by HV military and Croatian civil police." The 60 to 80 per cent there, does that not indicate that the 60 to 80 per cent of the property was burned starting on the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you agree with me that the report you filed on 26th of August says that the 60 to 80 per cent of the property which was systematically destroyed mainly by burning, is a reference to property that is being systematically destroyed as of the 7th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I read it different, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether you read it different or not is -- let me -- Mr. Misetic puts a question to the witness and if the witness's reading is different then he'll tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, but it shouldn't also be a mischaracterization of what on its face appears to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there is any problem there the Chamber may exercise its supervisory function as well. For the time being, the question stands. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The summary, I believe, is a factual description, so that means that by the 24th of August, that was a rough estimate of the destruction in the former Sector South. That was a rough estimate of the -- and former Sector South of course is also the inner part of Sector South, away from the pink zone and that stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. My question specifically, though, is reading the first sentence, the context is that that destruction began on the 7th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we read the sentence: "In the period from 7th to 24th August, three ECMM teams observed a systematic destruction mainly by burning of property in the former RSK area." I can't make it more clinical/factual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, of course the text not unequivocally says that it was done after the 7th of August. That's exactly the reason why Mr. Misetic is putting the question to you, because the text as such does not give a direct answer. Now, your answering of this summary, 60 to 80 per cent to be destroyed, did you consider this to be destruction that has been inflicted after the 7th of August. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The destruction was inflicted during -- I mean, also the dates 4, 5, 6, we were not able to observe that. And up until the 24th of August. So, yes, by that time, the destruction had reached around that level, a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 60 to 80 per cent of the destruction as described in this report, you say, refers to destruction which was inflicted between the 4th and the 24th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- majority. It says roughly 60 to 80 per cent, which I understand anything between 55 and 85, the 60 to 80 per cent not to be taken as full precise, refers that to damage inflicted between the 4th and the 24th of August, or does it refer to other damage as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to try to finish this document and then we can take the break, Your Honour. If we could go eight pages in to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now in your own report you annexed as support for those conclusions, if we can look there in the middle and scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's the patrol you did on the 18th of August, with the findings. And then the patrol, the first trip we went through, the 22nd of August. Now, there are other patrols listed, but my question to you, sir, is you're the author of that report on the 26th, relying on your own findings of a daily report. You never went back and identified which of the villages you're attaching to support the conclusion are majority Croat villages that are destroyed, did you?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no -- in the summary, discussion of Croat villages or Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So then I'm correct. What you're trying to say is that the uniformed HV soldiers carrying this out were burning down Croat and Serb villages. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were burning down villages, as I observed it. Whether they were Croat or Serb villages, I observed burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So again, my specific question to you is your conclusion was the HV soldiers were burning down villages without with regard to the ethnic composition of the villages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- Mr. Misetic, irrespective of the composition of the population in 1991 because that isn't important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I mean to me it's semantics because on the eve of Operation Storm every village was majority Serb in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's -- you're not providing evidence. That may be what you -- we'll look at it in more detail. Again, it is the same question by Mr. Misetic. Is it your view in relation to this report that Croatian soldiers burned down villages even if the 1991 census tells us that these were -- at least at that time, by majority or sometimes even almost exclusively Croatian villages. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In some instances, villages were spared or towns were spared from destruction, even if they were Serb majority villages. I believe Mr. Misetic asked -- asked me to make that distinction between Croatian and Serbian villages. If I could please refer to the discussion in one of the reports where we have observed that some large village centres, irrespectable [sic] of their ethnic composition in 1991, 1995, were used to house certain people: Knin, Obrovac, Benkovac. So there is a mixed pattern, and I cannot, from these reports here, conclude whether this particular village was burned because it had Serbs or not. What we observed, we reported. I hope that satisfies the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is Mr. Misetic's question. Mr. Misetic, you may proceed. No, you may not proceed, because we'll have a break. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Misetic. The Chamber has received a submission by the Prosecution on the Defence -- on whether or not to admit a Defence exhibit. To say the least, that the submission shows some innovative or inventive aspects not only to express an expression of the view of the Prosecution whether or not to admit that exhibit, but is proffering a Prosecution Exhibit to replace what the Defence seeks to have admitted. Now I do understand that there this is some confusion about what the basis for such an approach is. I also understand that that aspect has not been dealt with a brief informal exchange of views between the parties. Of course, there is no issue that on the admissibility of that particular document that the Chamber's had, parties can make brief submissions, but of course the Chamber, at that time, did not envisage that the submissions would be of a kind which goes -- well, beyond what is usually discussed if we are discussing the admission of the admissibility of a document. So the Prosecution is invited to explain, in perhaps a short submission, explain the innovative, inventive way approach and what justifies such an approach under the present circumstances, and the Defence is invited to include in its short written submissions this aspect as well so that we have everything on the record. So the chamber has to deal with two issues at this moment: The first is admission of -- what was it? D568. And at the same time the new avenues that apparently the Prosecution wants to find, again inventive, innovative, but not yet fully explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think Mr. Tieger just made an e-mail shortly after 4.00 explaining in a few sentences, but perhaps not detailed enough the innovative approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that of course, apparently, if I understand Mr. Misetic well, is one of the concerns that he expressed, that he is uncertain about the procedural basis on which this approach is taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. We will do that as soon we can, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I would note, Your Honour, two things. One, I have not had an opportunity to see Mr. Tieger's e-mail; and second, I assume that we will be given an opportunity to respond to the submission that the Prosecution makes rather than filing simultaneous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll wait for another second to respond and then include that in your response. I can't imagine that you had not received the reply because it is from --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I didn't say I didn't receive it. I just don't have my e-mail open at the moment, so I haven't read it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was three minutes past 4.00. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, continuing where we left off. I want -- you were invited by the Prosecution to make an assessment and so that's why I'm usually not quick to ask witnesses for their assessments, but let me ask you: You made the assessment that what the Croatians -- Croatian forces did in August 1995 was much more professional than what happened -- what the Serbs did between 1991 and 1995. My question to you is: Was part of the professional operation that was conducted, in your view, to burn down villages regardless of the ethnic composition of the village as reflected in the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to "professional operation," what I meant was the ability to maintain command and control, to maintain speed of operation, to secure what perhaps be -- be aims. Now, I made a reference to the RSK's abilities for the same, and in that comparison, I felt that the Croatian armed forces were considerable [sic] more professional. We have dealt with the lack of NCOs and that stuff, so I will not dwell upon that, yesterday. With regard to burning down villages, my assessment is based on the observation in the weeks that followed Operation Storm, where, to my mind, the conduct of formations -- sorry, the conduct of soldiers in what I considered formations was, as I said, controlled and executed. This included also the burning down of property.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Let me stop you right there, because that is the point I want to get to. And that means it included property in villages which were majority Croat per the 1991 census. That's your assessment. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assessment was and is that the burning was executed to a considerable degree initially, after Operation Storm, in what would appear to me as being an operational fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That doesn't answer my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it doesn't. And the reason is that I did not distinguish between Serb and Croat villages. I did in the pause here, in the break, have a chance to think of your previous questions, and I have to state that the observations in the daily reports and the discussions we did in the longer reports, we did not pinpoint this village was burned by -- this village was a Serb village or a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, would -- wouldn't that have been an important thing to do as you were making an assessment as you did in the report of the 26th of August, in trying to figure out what was going on in the sector, sir?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There could be a lot of things what one could wish to do in the 22nd -- 26th of August report, but what is on print is what we see. And I don't recall that I say that 60 to 80 per cent of the property is Serb and is burned by Croats, and I don't develop that line there. If could you please indicate to me where in the report you suggest that I say that. I would also bring to the attention the discussion I have in the 100-day report where it is also said that this wanton destruction made it difficult for the Croatian government to execute its ambitious plan for return.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is actually a point that I wanted to get into with you later. Let me understand that point. You do make that point in your 100-day survey, sir, is that this burning actually obstructed the ambitious Croatian plan to return displaced persons, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we can just have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you just said it, sir --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You just said.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my thought, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now what I don't understand is how you reconcile the fact that one the one hand you say that all of this destruction was done systematically by the Croatians army on the one hand, and on the other hand you also share the conclusion that this burning obstructed Croatian plans? How do you reconcile those two things?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I discuss exactly that point in my report, that what could be the reasons for that, what were the official point, what we observed, it is it a very, very good question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm posing it to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And can I only say that in such an answer I can only repeat the discussion that is here in the reference material.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, sir. Here's the point. You have come here and you've told us -- let me finish the question, please. You had three days with the Prosecution through which you made it crystal clear that it's your view that the burning that took place in August was done by professional soldiers acting under command in units. At the same time, you also say that this burning frustrated the Croatian plans to return displaced persons to the area. Is it your position that the Croatian government simultaneously executed a plan to burn down areas in order to frustrate its own plans to return displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the question is unclear tell us; otherwise, please, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in three days of direct testimony, you made it crystal clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just a minor point. It wasn't three days of direct testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. And at the same time it doesn't assist very much on how much time he's, but your testimony was as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On direct examination, yes. On direct examination, Mr. Liborius, you testified that it is your view that the destruction that occurred in August 1995 after Operation Storm was systematically done by HV troops acting under command. You also have now told the Court and repeated what you say in your 100-day survey, which is that you believe this burning frustrated the plans of the Croatian government to return displaced persons to the area. My question is simple: Is it your view that the Croatian government, A, executed a plan to burn down villages while -- which simultaneously frustrated its own plans to return displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would be fair to show the piece quoted in the 100-day report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He just testified to it Judge, I don't need to show him anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Because you put it to him, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough. Let me just check a few things because the question is ... Yes, you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Croatian plan to return the displaced persons became an issue locally; we detected that in our monitoring activity throughout the Autumn. If I'm now asked to elaborate on -- on why this burning took place, I can give you my thoughts now. They correspond to a vast degree to -- to reporting, that this must have been in an attempt to reduce the amount of property. Perhaps reduce the possibilities for Serbs who have fled to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That doesn't answer my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me try to see. Mr. Liborius, Mr. Misetic - and please correct me when I did not understand you correctly - just wants to know whether it's your testimony that on the one hand side, Croatian government wanted Croats to return, and, at the same time, that it was Croatian government policy to cause so much destruction that that would not be possible anymore. Is that -- I try to simplify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to use his own words which is at line 18, page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You just said: "I would bring to the attention the discussion I have in the 100-day report where it is also said that this destruction made it difficult for the Croatian government to execute its ambitious plan for return." Those are your words just now. My question is very simple: Is it your position that the destruction was inflicted under a Croatian plan, which made it difficult for the Croatian government to implement its own plan of return?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you take into consideration that large town centres were spared, then it makes sense. If you destroy the countryside, you maintain the larger population centres, and then you have a situation where you can still populate it to a certain degree in the larger town centres. That is exactly the discussion I conduct in some of the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's not what you say, though, sir.
